topic: PMB: Local Memory for Coding Agents That Proves It's Used

key_points: PMB (oleksiijko/pmb) is a local-first, MCP-native memory layer for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf, Zed, VS Code, gemini, opencode, continue).
Core pitch: 'Your AI agent forgets every session. PMB gives it memory, on your disk.' One SQLite file is the source of truth; LanceDB holds rebuildable vector indexes beside it.
No API keys, no cloud, no telemetry, no LLM call on the read path. Apache 2.0. pip install pmb-ai.
Headline differentiator: it tells you WHEN memory is actually helping instead of claiming '+X%' — via Earned Memory / follow-rate scoring.
Recall ~35ms warm (p50), p95 110ms; prepare() 4-16ms; record_batch_async <1ms; MCP cold boot 3.7s.
LoCoMo recall@10 = 94.5% (n=10); multilingual top-10 = 99.2% (900-query mega-stress).
Hybrid recall: BM25 + dense vector + entity graph + optional cross-encoder rerank, fused via Reciprocal-Rank-Fusion.

Hooks at the protocol level (UserPromptSubmit auto-recall, PostToolUse ambient observe, SessionStart session-restore, Stop follow-through + ambient auto-write) so the model never has to remember to call a tool.
Dashboard (127.0.0.1:8765) with Map (live entity graph), Timeline (git-graph journal), and 9 tabs incl. Lessons (per-rule follow-rate, dead-lesson detection), Duplicates, Performance, Recall.
Multilingual out of the box: paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 covers 50+ languages; a Russian query finds an English fact.
105 tunables (25 default-tier, 80 hidden behind --pro).
Secrets auto-redacted at write time (OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS/Stripe/GitHub keys).
296 GitHub stars, 23 forks, 3 open issues, Python, created 2026-05-25 (as of 2026-08-24).
Quickstart: pip install pmb-ai; pmb setup; pmb warmup; pmb stats; pmb recall; pmb doctor.
pmb connect wires one or more agents to one workspace (all stdio, server runs as child of agent — no network, no port, no token).
Two agents can share one memory via same workspace; SQLite WAL + 10s busy-timeout handle concurrent writes.
Optional HTTP mode with bearer-token auth for team/multi-machine sharing (docs/guide/TEAM.md).

Dedup: 4 layers — exact text match -> cosine >=0.92 auto-merge -> 0.80-0.92 borderline (LLM verify later) -> manual review in dashboard. Old values archived, never deleted; keyed_fact_as_of(t) for time-travel.

Ambient memory (write side): journals the agent's work even when it forgets record_batch; outcome-scored (tests passed, failure fixed, deploy ran), tagged source=autowrite, reversible with pmb forget-auto. On by default.

Self-improvement loop: every surfaced lesson carries a surface_id; follow-through recorded both by agent confirm (mark_lesson_followed) and Stop-hook inference. Lessons tab shows USEFUL (followed>=2x), UNVERIFIED, DEAD (ignored>=2).
Privacy: 100% offline by default, zero telemetry, workspace under ~/.pmb/<name>/, copyable/exportable. pmb export dumps to Markdown/JSON.
Roadmap: litestream backup, optional cloud-sync (BYO bucket), tree-sitter project indexing, image OCR.
'Does PMB actually help?' — PMB measures its own value conservatively, on your data, and says loudly when the signal isn't trustworthy yet.

Two questions, two methods: (1) Retrieval quality via reproducible benchmarks (LoCoMo recall@10 ~94.5%, multilingual top-10 ~99.2%); (2) Outcome impact via Earned Memory, joining each surfaced lesson to the turn's outcome (tests pass/fail, red->green, build, deploy — no LLM).

Earned Memory reports at three levels of rigor: Associational lift (weakest, confounded — lessons surface on harder turns so a helpful lesson can show negative lift; a flag for review, never ground truth); Statistical honesty (95% Wilson CI, useful/harmful only when CI clears baseline AND n>=min_n, else unverified/insufficient); Within-lesson causal read (strongest — same lesson followed vs ignored, holding the surfacing trigger fixed).
An n=1 fluke can never read as a real effect.

Earned Memory is measurement-only: it does NOT feed ranking or decay until the outcome signal is dense enough to trust. PMB would rather show 'insufficient' than let a flattering-but-wrong number re-weight memory.
Run on your own data: pmb health lessons-impact -w 90. Seeing 'signal: insufficient' early is the honest answer, not a bug.
Show HN: PMB — 26 points, 9 comments (2026-06-29).
Commenter calls for a 'memory arena' to list all agent-memory projects (hundreds) and objectively compare/score them against each other and vanilla harnesses like Claude Code.
Concern: 'My main concern is that it can overwhelm the context window with useless facts' — the context-bloat risk is the top user worry.
Skeptic: '35ms local aint a brag... arent there tonnes of agent memory options so why is this different from those?' — differentiation pressure.
One user reported the pmbai.dev site intermittently failing to load (secure connection error) — a reliability nit.
Author (oleksiibond) points to the repo for under-the-hood inspection.
deja-vu — closest category cousin: memory for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor + 17 others); indexes sessions agents already wrote to disk, including months before install.
No LLM, no embeddings, one local Go binary; MIT; 693 stars; 85.3% hit@1 on LongMemEval-S, 69.6% on LoCoMo, sub-ms lookups over 5GB.
P2P sync over SSH is its headline differentiator; only data records sync, not instructions; known secrets deleted at indexing.
Contrast with PMB: deja-vu is retroactive verbatim-text search (BM25) with no follow-through measurement; PMB adds proactive hooks, entity graph, and honest impact scoring.
Beads by Steve Yegge — 'A memory upgrade for your coding agent'; Go; 26,551 stars; the reference point for the category.
Persists and recalls decisions across sessions; high-profile HN launch and strong community traction.
Contrast: Beads is the category heavyweight by stars; PMB differentiates on local-first SQLite, MCP-native hooks, and honest follow-through measurement rather than raw adoption.

stats.fact: PMB recall is ~35ms warm (p50), 110ms p95; prepare() returns in 4-16ms; record_batch_async writes return in <1ms; MCP cold boot is 3.7s.
PMB scores LoCoMo recall@10 = 94.5% (n=10) and multilingual top-10 = 99.2% on a 900-query mega-stress eval.
PMB's default embedder (paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2) covers 50+ languages; top-1 = 1.00 for en/fr/pt/ru on a 101-query eval.
PMB repo has 296 GitHub stars, 23 forks, 3 open issues as of 2026-08-24; created 2026-05-25; Python; Apache 2.0.
PMB's Show HN post reached 26 points and 9 comments on 2026-06-29.
PMB has 105 configurable settings: 25 default-tier keys that affect day-to-day quality, 80 advanced knobs hidden behind --pro.
PMB dedup uses 4 layers: exact text match -> cosine >=0.92 auto-merge -> 0.80-0.92 borderline (LLM verify later) -> manual review in dashboard; old values archived, never deleted.
PMB dashboard binds to 127.0.0.1:8765 only; workspace lives under ~/.pmb/<name>/; 100% offline by default with zero telemetry.
PMB's Earned Memory uses a 95% Wilson confidence interval and only labels a lesson useful/harmful when the CI clears baseline AND n>=min_n; otherwise unverified/insufficient.
PMB auto-redacts secrets at write time (OpenAI/Anthropic/AWS/Stripe/GitHub keys, configurable).
Category context: Beads (Steve Yegge) has 26,551 stars; deja-vu has 693 stars and 85.3% hit@1 on LongMemEval-S.

angles: The 'proves it's used' differentiator: PMB is one of the few agent-memory tools that measures whether memory actually changes outcomes (Earned Memory: associational lift -> Wilson CI -> within-lesson causal read), instead of claiming '+X%'. This is the review's core hook.

Context-bloat is the #1 user fear: hooks auto-inject memory before the model thinks, so the risk is overwhelming the context window with useless facts — PMB's answer is follow-rate scoring + dead-lesson detection + trivial-message filtering.
Local-first trust: one SQLite file you own, no cloud, no telemetry, secrets auto-redacted, Apache 2.0 — vs hosted memory services. Privacy as a selling point.

Hooks vs 'remember to call a tool': the hard part of agent memory isn't storing, it's getting the agent to USE it. PMB wires hooks at the protocol level (auto-recall, ambient observe, session-restore, follow-through) so the model never has to remember.

Honest measurement philosophy: 'A memory system you can't measure is one you can't trust.' PMB refuses to let a flattering-but-wrong number re-weight memory — measurement-only until the signal is dense.

Category landscape: hundreds of agent-memory projects (Beads, deja-vu, ctx, mem0, zep, Mnemos, NexusMem, Mimirs, CodeYam). PMB is young (296 stars) — position honestly as a promising niche tool with a unique measurement angle, not a category leader.
Multilingual recall as a differentiator: 50+ languages out of the box, no language packs; a Russian query finds an English fact.
Practical workflow: quickstart (7 commands), pmb connect for multi-agent shared memory, dashboard for inspection/editing, pmb export for portability.
